version.changelog:
No file changes detected.

- This version does not include any changes to code or documentation.  
- All features, usage rules, and behavior remain the same as the previous release.

llm.summary: This is a disclosed social-media lookup skill that sends user searches and an auth token to fixed external API endpoints, with no evidence of hidden or destructive behavior.

dimensions.detail: The code and documentation consistently support keyword and company/domain social-media lookup across LinkedIn, Facebook, Twitter/X, and Instagram.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The skill sends user-provided keywords, company names, domains, selected platform names, and an AuthToken to api.topeasychina.com; this is purpose-aligned and documented, though privacy disclosure could be more prominent.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Artifacts are normal skill files: manifest, documentation, a handler, and an API wrapper. No installer script, package installation, or automatic mutation mechanism was found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime access is limited to Node.js, reading the documented TPAgent.key auth token file, and POST requests to two hardcoded whitelisted API URLs.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill repeatedly reads TPAgent.key so paid status can refresh, but it does not write files, create background workers, spawn processes, or request elevated privileges.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable sending search terms, company names, domains, platform selections, and the TPAgent.key authorization token to api.topeasychina.com. Avoid submitting confidential prospecting lists or sensitive business research unless that third-party service is acceptable for your data handling needs.
llm.findings: [SQP-2] expected: The external POST data flow is real, but it is coherent with the search function and disclosed in the API/config documentation; treat it as a privacy notice rather than evidence of hidden behavior.
